data.title: EVERolimus effectiveness after proGREssion on ENdocrine therapy plus CDK4/6 inhibitor for ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer: EVERGREEN study
data.authors: Martins-Branco D; Lobo-Martins S; Aftimos P; Pereira B; Vasconcelos de Matos L; Fernandes L; Campôa E; Nader-Marta G; Moreau M; Taylor D; Duhoux FP; Simões P; Garcia AR; Patel V; Confente C; Alpuim Costa D; Pereira J; Santos C; Paesmans M; Sarmento F; Gantes Padrão T; Simão D; Bandarra D; Sousa B; Brito M; Gombos A; Ameye L; de Azambuja E

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Everolimus added to endocrine therapy provided modest but statistically significant PFS benefit (5.0 vs 4.3 months; HR 0.68) in ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer post-CDK4/6 inhibitor progression, without demonstrable OS benefit, supporting selective use. Retrospective and non-randomised, so treatment-selection bias cannot be excluded.
data.abstract_excerpt: Multicentre, international, retrospective quasi-experimental study (n=207 women with ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression). Everolimus + endocrine therapy (n=150) vs endocrine therapy alone (n=57). Median real-world PFS: 5.0 vs 4.3 months (adjusted HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.47-0.99). Time to everolimus failure: 4.2 months. No significant differences in time to chemotherapy or overall survival. Safety profile consistent with prior reports. Median follow-up 31.8 months.

extracted_findings.effect: Modest PFS improvement (HR 0.68) in post-CDK4/6i ER+ breast cancer; no OS benefit demonstrated
